new_candidates.trigger: County currently lacks local zoning regulations for data centers, battery energy storage systems, or large-scale solar; officials cite fire hazards (BESS), noise/vibration from cooling units, light pollution, water/air quality, stormwater runoff, and traffic impacts.

The Vilas County Zoning & Planning Committee held a public hearing on the proposed ordinance on 2026-09-23 (the date of this research); the full County Board of Supervisors is scheduled to vote at its October 27, 2026 meeting. As drafted, the moratorium would freeze acceptance, review, or approval of development permits for data centers, BESS, and solar energy systems exceeding one acre, for 12 months, with exemptions for solar installations of one acre or less, ordinary maintenance/repairs, emergency utility restoration, and projects already holding valid county permits.

new_candidates.legal_basis: Town of Cassville (Grant County) data center ban ordinance, adopted using newly authorized village/zoning powers (ordinance number not located in reviewed sources)
new_candidates.trigger: A proposed roughly $1 billion, approximately 500-acre data center campus by an undisclosed developer (drawn by the town's proximity to the Cardinal-Hickory Creek high-voltage transmission line); residents opposed the secrecy and scale of the project and mobilized to give the town board zoning authority to block it.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; enacted April 16, 2026. Prohibits data centers in the town for up to two years and also restricts land-use changes (e.g., building a residence on farmland) without town board approval. The county cannot preempt the town's zoning authority in this instance. As of the reporting reviewed, the previously scouted developer had gone quiet, with no application filed.
new_candidates.affected_projects: An anonymous developer's proposed ~$1 billion, 400-500 megawatt data center campus (roughly 500 acres) near the Cardinal-Hickory Creek transmission line; the developer reportedly went quiet after the town's action and was also considering sites in Indiana and North Dakota.
new_candidates.outcome: Town electors authorized village/zoning powers and the Town Board adopted a two-year ban on data centers, blocking the proposed project.

evidence.title: In rural Wisconsin, a town rejects a plan to build a massive data center
evidence.supports: Detailed, on-the-ground account of the April 16, 2026 electors' vote (44-0) authorizing zoning power, the same-evening ordinance banning data centers for up to two years, and the specific project it targeted.
evidence.quote: The board of the town of Cassville, in Grant County, Wisconsin, discussed an ordinance on April 16, 2026, that would ban data centers in the township. That evening, town electors authorized the town supervisors to exercise zoning authority. ... The unanimous outcome — 44 ballots in favor of banning data centers, none against ... Cassville's new ordinance prohibits data centers in the town for up to two years and prevents land use changes, such as constructing a residence on a farm field, without the town board's approval.

new_candidates.trigger: Plan Commission and Village Board wanted to get ahead of potential data center proposals and avoid being "surprised"; part of a wave of similar actions among nearby Fox Valley/Northeast Wisconsin municipalities.

new_candidates.legal_basis: Proposed Milwaukee Common Council ordinance imposing a one-year data center moratorium, sponsored by Alderwoman Marina Dimitrijevic with Alex Brower, Russell W. Stamper II, and Robert Bauman; endorsed by the Zoning Code Technical Committee August 10, 2026
new_candidates.trigger: Milwaukee's zoning code does not currently treat data centers as a distinct land use; sponsor wants rules in place before a major data center proposal is submitted, following controversy over a since-withdrawn data center component of a Midtown Center Walmart-site redevelopment.
new_candidates.current_status: Pending as of 2026-09-23. The City Plan Commission is scheduled to hold its hearing and make a recommendation on September 28, 2026; the proposal still requires Common Council approval before taking effect. If adopted, the moratorium would bar city departments/boards/commissions from accepting or processing most new data center applications for one year after passage or until the zoning code is amended to specifically regulate data centers, whichever is first, with an exception for planned-development-district properties and a proposed (contested) tribal-land exemption for the Forest County Potawatomi Community.
new_candidates.affected_projects: A 19,000-square-foot "computer research facility" that opponents characterized as a data center was initially part of a proposed Midtown Center (former Walmart site) redevelopment; the developer later removed it from the plan.
new_candidates.outcome: Zoning Code Technical Committee endorsed the proposed one-year data center moratorium (Aug. 10, 2026); City Plan Commission hearing scheduled Sept. 28, 2026; Common Council vote still required.
